## Board Manifest: mouse-joystick-pcb

Single-axis mouse joystick: RP2040 with GPIO isolation, one TMC5130A, torque bridge, brake current sink, analog angle output, InstrumentPort-Digital-50 taps, 36 V protected input with 12 V and 5 V regulators; v1.0 as built.

**Project:** `mouse-joystick-pcb.kicad_pro` **Netclass profiles:** `hv-power-24v`, `instrument-taps` **Datum:** aux axis origin at KiCad (137.425, 95) mm **Placements:** 15; **board sheets:** 4; **nets:** 76; **open ports:** 36

This document records this board's RP2040 GPIO allocation. It covers **two
scopes at once**: what Rev 0 populates, and the full scope that later revisions
grow into. The InstrumentPort-Digital-50 profile itself belongs in
`board-interfaces` and is not redefined here.

## Rev 0 Is A Strict Subset

Rev 0 was scaled back to get testable hardware in the researcher's hands sooner.
See `docs/rev0-plan.md` for what it contains and why.

The allocation below is written so that **no pin moves between Rev 0 and full
scope**. Rev 0 populates 18 of the 24 allocated GPIOs; the other 6 are reserved,
routed nowhere, and become live in later revisions without disturbing anything
Rev 0 established. Firmware written against Rev 0 keeps working.

`GP24` `~{INSTR_BUF_OE}` became live on 2026-08-16 when the InstrumentPort moved
into Rev 0; it was already allocated and already in the bypass group. The same
day, `GP14`-`GP16` and `GP18` left the allocation entirely when the encoder and
limit switch stopped reaching the MCU, which is why the denominator dropped from
29 to 25. **`GP14` came back on 2026-08-17** as `HV_DIAG_EN`, taking the
denominator to 26. **`GP12` and `GP17` left it on 2026-08-26** when the analog
output block was built against a part with no `LDAC` or `CLR` pin, which takes
the denominator to 24 and leaves six spares.

That property is not free, and it cost exactly one trade — see
[The Bus Switch Costs A Pin](#the-bus-switch-costs-a-pin).

## RP2040 GPIO Allocation

Checked against RP2040 peripheral pin muxing. `UART0` is the pyControl link,
`SPI0` serves the TMC5130A, `SPI1` serves the **torque ADC**, and `I2C0` serves
the **two DAC blocks** at 0x48 and 0x49. Chip selects are plain GPIO, not
hardware `CSn` — RP2040's PL022 hardware chip select does not hold `CS` low
across the TMC5130A's 40-bit multi-byte datagrams, and the ADS8689's
`CONVST/CS` both starts the conversion and frames the read, so firmware needs
direct control of its timing.

**`SPI1 SCK` exists only on `GP10`, `GP14` and `GP26`**, and 14 and 26 are
spent. That single constraint is why the freed DAC-SPI pins became the torque
bus and the I2C pair moved to `GP16`/`GP17` rather than the other way round.

The `rp2040_with_gpio_isolation_sn74cb3q3245` block exposes these as **two**
label banks: raw `GPIO0`-`GPIO8` and `GPIO10`-`GPIO29`, and switched `ISO0`-`ISO8`
and `ISO10`-`ISO29`. There is no `GPIO9`, no `ISO9` and no `~{OE}` port — `GP9`
is consumed inside the block. The ADC pins are plain `GPIO26`-`GPIO29`, not the
old `GPIO26_ADC0` names.

**Iso** column: `sw` = wire the board net to the block's `ISOn` pin, so the
signal crosses the bus switch; `byp` = wire it to the raw `GPIOn` pin. **Per
index they are the same node whenever the bus is enabled — use one or the
other, never both.** The rule is the powered domain of the far end, not
convenience — see [GPIO Isolation](#gpio-isolation).

**Dir** column: direction **as seen by the RP2040**. `out` = the MCU drives it,
`in` = the MCU reads it. This is also the KiCad shape to give the matching
hierarchical pin on the `mcu` sheet — `out` → Output, `in` → Input. See
[Signal Direction And Sheet Pin Types](#signal-direction-and-sheet-pin-types).

The allocation table itself is generated from `kicad/board.yaml`'s `nets` (the
`gpio` and `meaning` of every MCU net) into
[`docs/generated/gpio-allocation.md`](generated/gpio-allocation.md) by `make
docs`, with the class and every block or sheet port each net reaches; it
replaced the hand-written table here on 2026-10-13. The numbered notes below
are what its meanings cite, and the **Iso** and **Dir** reading above still
applies: a net whose meaning says "via the bus switch" is switched, one that
does not bypasses it, and "out" or "in" is the direction as the MCU sees it.

¹ Rev 0 lands `FW_TRIG0`/`FW_TRIG1` on `TRIG0`/`TRIG1` of the InstrumentPort.
They are the cheapest bring-up instrumentation on the board and the natural
trigger source for a long capture. They were also to get labelled test points;
**as of 2026-08-17 no test points exist on the board** — see [Test Points —
Outstanding](#test-points--outstanding).

² `~{BUS_SW_EN}` **is driven only inside the MCU block.** `GP9` drives all four
`~OE` inputs plus the 7.87 kΩ pull-up inside
`rp2040_with_gpio_isolation_sn74cb3q3245`, so the board must **never drive it** —
the pull-up is the only thing defining the reset state, and a second driver
fights the MCU. **A read-only port was added to the block on 2026-09-17**, shape
`output`, so a capture can witness the isolation state on `DIG27`. It is a
declaration, not a connection: the netlist still shows exactly six nodes on that
net (`R40006`, `GP9`, and the four `~OE` pins). Because the port is an `output`
on both sides of the sheet boundary, ERC reports a pin conflict if anything on
the board ever tries to drive it. The `mcu` sheet still needs the matching pin.
See [InstrumentPort-Digital-50 Pinout](#instrumentport-digital-50-pinout).

`SW_RAIL_SENSE_DIV_2`.

Earlier text called it `R502`; that number now belongs to a USB-C `CC`
pull-down. The block's port is named `DIAG_ENABLE`, not `HV_DIAG_EN` — the
`HV_` prefix is the board's, applied at the root. See the note on `DIAG_EN`

soft reset writes `0x1010` to `TRIGGER`. Both functions survive; they cost zero

this footnote any more** — `GP12` and `GP17` were re-spent in v1.0 — but the

The freed `GP10`/`GP11` plus `GP12` became the torque ADC's `SPI1`, and

both are spent on the UART through `R301`/`R302`. There is no third or fourth
line, and the board's only BNC is `J1101` (`ANGLE_OUT`), so `PYC_PULL_EVENT`,
`PYC_FAULT` and `PYC_RSYNC_IN` **have no physical destination on this board**.
They stay allocated so no pin moves, and the two outputs are still worth
observing on the InstrumentPort, but `PYC_RSYNC_IN` has no source and gets no
channel. Either add connectors in a later revision or retire the three.
**`PYC_RSYNC_IN` is now retired — decided 2026-09-18.** Its `GP23` was spent on
`~{HV_FAULT}`, which had to vacate an ADC pin. Of the three it was the right one
to take: it is the only one with no source *and* no instrument channel, while
`PYC_PULL_EVENT` and `PYC_FAULT` are outputs still worth observing. `GP20` and
`GP22` remain reserved for those two.

DUT block is default-enabled with both `~OE` inputs held low and no port, so
`~{INSTR_BUF_OE}` no longer exists. Its pull-up circuit and firmware init are
deleted rather than ported. See
[the migration plan](digital-instrument-port-migration.md).

¹⁰ **Added 2026-09-16, and this pin was owed since 2026-09-02.** The
`TPS1HTC100-Q1`'s `LATCH` was strapped high through a 1 kΩ `RPROT` until the
bench showed that latch-off and power-up are in direct conflict on this board:
the switch trips relative thermal shutdown 1-2 ms into charging `+36V_SW`'s
208 µF, so **auto-retry is the only mechanism that can bring the rail up at
all**. `docs/power.md` → [`LATCH` — Tie It High For
Latch-Off](power.md#latch--tie-it-high-for-latch-off) recorded the fix as
"`LATCH` on a spare GPIO" but no pin was ever allocated here; this is that
allocation. **Drive it low for the power-up ramp and high once the rail is
established** — that buys retry-based soft-start *and* latch-off, and the
device's internal 0.7-1.3 MΩ pull-down makes auto-retry the default whenever the
MCU is unpowered or in reset, which is exactly when the rail has to be able to
charge. Do not strap it either way. The 1 kΩ `RPROT` is `R503` **inside** the HV
input block, so the board owes only the wiring.

¹¹ **The ADC reshuffle, 2026-09-18.** Only `GP26`-`GP29` can reach the ADC, and
`~{HV_FAULT}` — a digital open-drain input — was occupying `GP29`/ADC3. It moved
to `GP23`, spending the `PYC_RSYNC_IN` reservation (footnote 8) and freeing ADC3.
`GP27`/ADC1 and `GP29`/ADC3 are now **assigned** to `BRAKE_ISENSE` and
`ANGLE_OUT_MON` respectively, and both **bypass** the isolation switch — see
[The Rule](#the-rule-follow-the-far-ends-power-domain). **The `~{HV_FAULT}` move is
wired, and so are both monitors** — verified at `U601` pins 39 and 41. Levels, source impedances, the sheet pins still owed and the accuracy
limits are in [The Four ADC Channels, And The v1.0 Analog
Readback](#the-four-adc-channels-and-the-v10-analog-readback).

**v1.0: 29 connected (27 with a destination, 2 reserved per footnote 8), 0 spare,
1 internal (`GP9`).** **The MCU is now fully allocated — there is no spare GPIO
left.** Updated twice on 2026-09-18: the line read 25 with a destination, 3
reserved and 1 spare before `~{HV_FAULT}` moved onto `GP23` (retiring
`PYC_RSYNC_IN` and freeing `GP29`), and the last two went to `BRAKE_ISENSE` and
`ANGLE_OUT_MON`. **If more pins are
ever needed, retiring the remaining two footnote-8 signals is the cheapest
reclaim available** — they have no connector, so nothing on the board changes.

**Switched: 15 channels** — `ISO2`-`ISO8`, `ISO10`-`ISO13`, `ISO15`-`ISO18`.
**Bypass: 13** — `GPIO0`, `GPIO1`, `GPIO14`, `GPIO19`-`GPIO26`, `GPIO28`,
`GPIO29`. The remaining 30 block pins get no-connect flags: the 15 raw pins
whose index is switched, `GPIO27`, and the 14 unused `ISO` pins (`ISO0`, `ISO1`,
`ISO14`, `ISO19`-`ISO29`).

**Verified against the schematic 2026-09-16.** Every switched signal sits on its
index-matched `ISO` pin and every bypass signal on the matching raw `GPIO` pin,
checked at pad level through the netlist — `~{TMC_CS}` on `ISO2` through
`TQ_CAL_EN` on `ISO18`, and `GPIO0`/`GPIO1`/`GPIO14`/`GPIO19`/`GPIO21`/`GPIO25`/
`GPIO26`/`GPIO28`/`GPIO29` on the raw side. Note that a raw `GPIOn` net always
shows **two** nodes at the RP2040 end — the MCU pad and the switch's `B` pin —
because the block wires all 29 channels 1:1 internally. That is the block
working as designed, not a stray connection.

**Four pins were freed on 2026-08-16** and the allocation went from comfortable to
roomy. That matters for more than tidiness — see the note on rev 2 below. One of
the four, `GP14`, was spent again on 2026-08-17.

**Two more were freed on 2026-08-26**, and unlike every earlier reclaim these
cost nothing at all. `GP12` and `GP17` were not traded away or descoped — the
part chosen for the analog output simply does not have the pins they were
reserved for. That is the difference between this reclaim and the
`TMC_REF_STIM` trade below, and it is why the rev 2 arithmetic changes sign.

`DIAG_EN` on the input block's switch is on **`GP14`, through `R502` 10 kΩ**.
**Reversed 2026-08-17**; earlier guidance said tie it to `+3.3V`, not to a GPIO,
because diagnostics have no reason to be gated and tying it costs no pin. That
reasoning was right about diagnostics and wrong about the cost. Held high, the
`TPS1HTC100-Q1`'s OFF-state open-load detection keeps an internal ~150 kΩ pull-up
from `VS` to `VOUT` permanently enabled (`ROL_OFF` 110-166 kΩ), injecting ~240 µA
into `+36V_SW`. Against that rail's ~208 µF the voltage creeps at ~1.2 V/s and
crosses the `TPSM365R6`'s 3.6 V minimum `VIN` in about 3 s, so the buck starts,
collapses, and hiccups — the switched domain never cleanly powers off. That
breaks the property that `HV_EN` power-cycles every resettable chip, and it
corrupts `SW_RAIL_SENSE`. `DIAG_EN` has an internal pull-down, so with `GP14`
high-Z at reset diagnostics are off and `+36V_SW` sits at true zero. Per the
device's Table 7-1 the current limit and thermal shutdown are unaffected by
`DIAG_EN` — only reporting is gated — so **firmware must raise `GP14` before
reading `HV_SNS` or `~{HV_FAULT}`**. Without it neither works at all; see
`docs/power.md`.

### The v1.0 GPIO Changes

Eight pins changed and one left the sheet. Nothing else moved, so firmware
written against Rev 0's bypass group, TMC bus and power-monitoring group keeps
working unchanged.

| Pin    | Rev 0 / rev 1               | v1.0                                                                                  | Why                                                                |
|--------|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `GP9`  | `~{BUS_SW_EN}`, board-wired | same signal, **internal to the block**, with a read-only monitor port from 2026-09-17 | the combined MCU block owns the enable and its pull-up             |
| `GP10` | `DAC_SPI_SCK`               | `TQ_SPI_SCK`                                                                          | DACs went I2C; `SPI1 SCK` exists nowhere else                      |
| `GP11` | `DAC_SPI_COPI`              | `TQ_SPI_COPI`                                                                         | same                                                               |
| `GP12` | spare                       | `TQ_SPI_CIPO`                                                                         | `SPI1 RX`                                                          |
| `GP13` | `~{DAC_CS}`                 | `~{BRAKE_FAULT}`                                                                      | I2C needs no chip select                                           |
| `GP15` | spare                       | `TQ_CONVST_CS`                                                                        | plain GPIO, timing-critical                                        |
| `GP16` | spare                       | `DAC_SDA`                                                                             | `I2C0` adjacent pair                                               |
| `GP17` | spare                       | `DAC_SCL`                                                                             | same                                                               |
| `GP18` | spare                       | `TQ_CAL_EN`                                                                           | plain GPIO                                                         |
| `GP24` | `~{INSTR_BUF_OE}`           | `HV_LATCH`                                                                            | digital-50 has no enable; the bench-proven latch pin took the slot |

**Net naming: COPI/CIPO, never MOSI/MISO or SDI/SDO.** Board net names and the
comments describing them use `COPI`/`CIPO` throughout. `SDI`/`SDO`/`SDIN` appear
in this document **only** where a device's own pin is meant — the TMC5130A's
`SDI`/`SDO` pins, the DAC80501's `SDIN`, the block ports of
`torque_bridge_0_3v3_ina821` — and those are quoted as-is because renaming a
datasheet pin would be worse than the inconsistency.

**That makes one mapping worth stating explicitly, because crossing it is
invisible to ERC and DRC:** at the parent sheet, board net `TQ_SPI_COPI` wires
to the torque block's **`SDI`** port and `TQ_SPI_CIPO` wires to its **`SDO`**
port. Both nets stay driven and terminated either way round, exactly like the
`AOUT`/`AOUT_MON` crossing that block family already warns about — verify it on
the netlist, not by eye. The same holds at the TMC: `TMC_SPI_COPI` → `SDI`,
`TMC_SPI_CIPO` → `SDO`, which the direction table further down already records.

**Two of the three analog monitors now reach the MCU — revised 2026-09-18.**
`ANGLE_OUT_MON` and `BRAKE_ISENSE` are assigned to `GP29`/ADC3 and `GP27`/ADC1;
see [The Four ADC
Channels](#the-four-adc-channels-and-the-v10-analog-readback). **`TQ_AOUT_MON`
still does not and does not need to** — torque arrives digitally over `SPI1`, so
digitising its analog monitor would add nothing, and there is no ADC channel left
anyway. None of the three goes near the digital-50 connector: it has no `AIN`
tail and the migration plan forbids putting slow analog into a CMOS port buffer,
so instrument access to all three is still by test point.

What changed the calculus for the other two is that neither had any readback at
all. DAC health over I2C `STATUS` tells you the DAC acknowledged a write, not
that the amplifier downstream of it produced a voltage; `BRAKE_ISENSE` had only
the digital `~{BRAKE_FAULT}` bit. The ADC is far too coarse to *measure* either —
see the accuracy note in that section — but it distinguishes a live chain from a
dead one, which nothing else on the board did.

### InstrumentPort-Digital-50 Pinout

**This is the only instrument-port pinout for v1.0**, and it is one table in
DUT-side pin order covering every contact. The 40-pin overlay that used to
follow was deleted on 2026-09-17; `board-interfaces/docs/instrument-port-40.md`
and the git history hold it for boards already built.

**Connector:** `J1301`, Hirose `FH12-50S-0.5SVA(54)`,
`OW-CONN-FH12-50S-0-5SVA-54` — 50 contacts, 0.5 mm pitch, vertical ZIF, 3.6 mm
closed height, straight-ended 0.30 ±0.05 mm FFC. Footprint
`orb_weaver_connectors:Hirose_FH12-50S-0.5SVA_1x50-4MP_P0.5mm_Vertical`.

**The board never wires a connector pin.** The design block
`instrument_port_digital_50_dut_ffc_boundary_vertical` owns `J1301`, the four
`SN74LV541A` buffers and their `~OE` pull-downs. What the board wires is the
block's ports: **`DIG0`-`DIG31`, all thirty-two present and every one shape
`input`**, plus `+3.3V` and `GND`. **Bind `+3.3V` to `+3.3V_MCU`**, the always-on
rail — a buffer on the switched rail cannot observe the domain it is powering
down with. So the `Strand` column below is what you connect in the schematic,
one row per sheet pin, and `Pin` and `Bank` are reference information for cable,
probe and skew work — `Bank` names the `SN74LV541A` that carries the channel.

The [checked observation-port map](../kicad/observation/port-map.md) traces
all 32 contacts through their output resistor, buffer and input tap, with
conditional MCU paths and passive bias facts. It is regenerated from exported
connectivity and the board-owned contract; see its limits before interpreting
reset or power-off readings.

**Read-only, and enabled by hardware with no way to disable it.** Both `~OE`
inputs of each package are held low by board resistors `R1301`-`R1304`, there
is no enable port, and nothing on this connector may be driven inward. **Every
unused input still has to be tied**, because `~OE` does not gate the input
stage — see [Board-Level Input Biases](#board-level-input-biases).

**Cable orientation remains an open risk rather than a settled fact.** The
mapping is correct *given* a reversing cable assembly, and no straight-ended FFC
has been bought or continuity-checked. Under a complete end-to-end reversal
ground still meets ground and channel order reverses (`DIGn` to `DIG31-n`); that
symmetry is a convenience, not evidence that a given cable is correct.

**Tap** column: `MCU` taps the always-on MCU net directly, `ISO` taps the
`ISO`/A side of the bus switch so the capture shows what the peripheral actually
receives, and `block` means a design block drives the net in its own domain. The
reasoning is in [Where Each Signal Is
Tapped](#where-each-signal-is-tapped).

| Strand  | Pin | Bank    | Board net        | Tap     | State                                                  |
|---------|-----|---------|------------------|---------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `DIG0`  | 2   | `U1301` | `FW_TRIG0`       | `MCU`   | wired — hold on the upstream marker freeze             |
| `DIG1`  | 3   | `U1301` | `FW_TRIG1`       | `MCU`   | wired — hold on the upstream marker freeze             |
| `DIG2`  | 5   | `U1301` | `PYC_UART_TX`    | `MCU`   | wired                                                  |
| `DIG3`  | 6   | `U1301` | `PYC_UART_RX`    | `MCU`   | wired                                                  |
| `DIG4`  | 8   | `U1301` | *unused*         | —       | tied to GND — `PYC_PULL_EVENT` retired                 |
| `DIG5`  | 9   | `U1301` | *unused*         | —       | tied to GND — `PYC_FAULT` retired                      |
| `DIG6`  | 11  | `U1301` | *unused*         | —       | tied to GND — spare                                    |
| `DIG7`  | 12  | `U1301` | *unused*         | —       | tied to GND — spare                                    |
| `DIG8`  | 14  | `U1302` | `TMC_SPI_SCK`    | `ISO`   | wired                                                  |
| `DIG9`  | 15  | `U1302` | `~{TMC_CS}`      | `ISO`   | wired                                                  |
| `DIG10` | 17  | `U1302` | `TMC_SPI_COPI`   | `ISO`   | wired                                                  |
| `DIG11` | 18  | `U1302` | `TMC_SPI_CIPO`   | `ISO`   | wired                                                  |

when the three phantom pyControl signals were retired — footnote 8 offered that
choice and the schematic took it. Every unused input is explicitly tied, which is
what the block requires.

**The eighteen grounds are deliberately not in this table, and they need no sheet
pin.** Pins 1, 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22, 25, 26, 29, 32, 35, 38, 41, 44, 47 and
50 are wired to `GND` inside the design block; the board supplies ground once,
through the block's single `GND` port, and the buffer supply once through its
`+3.3V` port. One row here is one sheet pin to wire.

One thing is still owed from outside: the `DIG0`/`DIG1` marker pair is not frozen
in `board-interfaces/docs/instrument-port-digital.md`,
so hold `FW_TRIG0`/`FW_TRIG1` until it is.

#### Why The Channels Are Grouped The Way They Are

**Regrouped 2026-09-18. Nine strands changed role; no signal moved between
banks.** The profile lays each bank out as `GND, signal, signal`, so channels
arrive in **pairs that share a gap with no ground between them** — pins (14,15),
(17,18), (20,21) and so on. Coupling inside a pair is much higher than across a
ground, so what sits next to what is a real choice, and
`board-interfaces/docs/instrument-port-digital.md`
designed the pair unit for it: *"Pairs suit UART TX/RX, I2C clock/data, encoder
A/B, and beacon clock/data."* That same paragraph is honest about the limit —
*"The two signals within a pair can still couple; nearby returns are not a
guarantee of impedance, crosstalk, or bandwidth."*

Four pairs broke the rule before this change and now do not:

| Pins | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 14,15 | `TMC_SPI_SCK` + its own `TMC_SPI_COPI` | `TMC_SPI_SCK` + `~{TMC_CS}` |
| 17,18 | `TMC_SPI_CIPO` + `~{TMC_CS}` | `TMC_SPI_COPI` + `TMC_SPI_CIPO` |
| 27,28 | `TQ_SPI_SCK` + its own `TQ_SPI_COPI` | `TQ_SPI_SCK` + `TQ_CONVST_CS` |
| 30,31 | `TQ_SPI_CIPO` + `TQ_CONVST_CS` | `TQ_SPI_COPI` + `TQ_SPI_CIPO` |
| 33,34 | `TQ_CAL_EN` + `DAC_SDA` | `TQ_CAL_EN` + `~{BRAKE_FAULT}` |
| 36,37 | `DAC_SCL` + `~{BRAKE_FAULT}` | `DAC_SDA` + `DAC_SCL` |

**A clock beside its own data was the one adjacency worth fixing.** Not because
it endangers the board — nothing on this connector drives anything, the port is
read-only into a high-Z analyser — but because the coupled pulse arrives exactly
at the instant that data line is sampled against that clock, so it corrupts the
*measurement* you would be taking. `COPI` beside `CIPO` is the better pairing:
both transition just after a clock edge, so a coupled glitch lands mid-window
where the margin is widest. Pairing `SCK` with a static chip-select removes the
correlation entirely.

**`DAC_SDA` and `DAC_SCL` are together for a different reason, and not to reduce
noise.** I2C is the least noise-sensitive traffic here — open-drain, pulled up
through 4.7 kΩ, RC-shaped edges at 100–400 kHz — so coupling between clock and
data is negligible either way. Pairing them matters because it vacates the two
slots the split occupied, which is what let `DAC_SDA` stop sitting beside
`TQ_CAL_EN` and `DAC_SCL` beside `~{BRAKE_FAULT}`, and because a two-wire bus
that is always decoded as a unit should travel as a unit.

**Magnitude, so this is not mistaken for a defect.** Nothing here is measured.
With ~5 ns `SN74LV541A` edges and ~1.5–2 ns one-way delay through ~300 mm of
FFC, the line is electrically short, so near-end crosstalk never saturates and
the coupled amplitude scales by roughly `2·T_prop/t_r ≈ 0.7`. With a ground
flanking every pair, the worst glitch is somewhere in the low hundreds of
millivolts against an analyser threshold near 1.5 V. **It will not flip a
captured bit from idle.** This is hygiene, done while the sheet pins were being
wired and the PCB had no traces, not a fix for an observed problem.

**The bank assignment was already right and did not change.** Each subsystem
sits entirely inside one `SN74LV541A`, so within-bus skew stays package-matched;
every one of the nine changes stayed inside its own bank. `U1303` carries three
subsystems only because a five-channel bus cannot fill a bank alone.

**The analyser imposes no constraint of its own.** `CH0`-`CH31` map one-to-one to
`DIG0`-`DIG31`, and nothing in `instrument-control` binds a signal type to a
channel index — capture takes channel indices as arguments and the beacon's
`--clock`/`--data` are explicit overrides. The "preferred SPI SCK overlay"-style
language in
`board-interfaces/docs/la5032-instrument-port-40-mapping.md`
belongs to the **legacy 40-pin** adapter; the digital-50 draft says outright that
`DIG` names are *"not fixed assignments to SPI, UART, or particular MCU pins."*
The only block-of-eight that matters is the buffer package on this board.

**Name the witnesses `PG_*`, not after the rail — this is a netclass trap, not
a style preference.** This board's netclass patterns include **`/+5V_*` →
`PWR_5V`**, a wildcard meant for `/+5V_SW` and `/+5V_MCU`. A net called
`+5V_SW_PGOOD` matches it and is silently graded as a 5 V power rail: 0.25 mm
clearance and a **0.5 mm minimum track width** on a status line carrying ≤1 µA,
in the most congested copper on the board. Renamed to `PG_5V` on 2026-09-18,
which matches no pattern and lands in `Default` at 0.2 mm. `PG_12V` is clear for
the same reason — every 12 V pattern is either exact (`+12V`, `/+12V`, `12V`,
`/12V`) or `*/`-prefixed, and there is no `/+12V_*`. Note `docs/power.md` calls
the rail `+12V`, not `+12V_SW`, so `+12V_SW_PGOOD` would have been wrong twice.

**Levels, so neither witness is re-derived.** `SN74LV541A` inputs are 0-5.5 V
independent of `V_CC` and its thresholds are 0.7/0.3 x `V_CC`, so `V_IH` is
2.31 V at 3.3 V and 2.52 V at the top of the 3.0-3.6 V range. The 12 V block
divides with `R18002` 10 kΩ / `R18003` 4.7 kΩ, giving **3.84 V** nominal and
3.67-4.01 V worst case — 1.5 V below the input maximum and 1.15 V above the
worst-case threshold, from a 3.2 kΩ source that is far inside the part's
100 ns/V transition limit. **`PG_5V` is the tighter of the two:** `hv_to_5v`
pulls up through `R13001` 10 kΩ with no divider, so its high level is the 5 V
rail itself, ~5.07 V worst case — 0.43 V from the 5.5 V maximum — at ~67 ns/V
against that 100 ns/V limit. Both legal; suspect `PG_5V` first if a witness
ever misreads.

**`DIG31` observes `PG_12V`.** The completed board connects it to
`U1304` input pin 2; `R1902`/`R1903` form the 10 kΩ/4.7 kΩ divider from
12 V. The earlier temporary ground tie is gone. `DIG30` observes `PG_5V`
through input pin 3 of the same buffer, with `R1701` pulling up to 5 V.
Both connector outputs use the buffer's `+3.3V_MCU` supply.

**Bias belongs on the functional side of each tap.** The
[checked bias inventory](../kicad/observation/port-map.md#passive-bias-inventory)
records the actual resistor paths. PYC_UART_TX and HV_DIAG_EN have no external
resistor path to a declared rail; their reset behavior needs the MCU/device
state and internal pulls. A switched-rail pull-up predicts a low bias only
under the stated settled-rail and high-impedance-driver assumptions. Neither
that expectation nor an input tied to GND makes an unpowered buffer's output
a valid logic reading.

### Board-Level Input Biases

> **Read with [`docs/instrument-port-tap-resistors.md`](instrument-port-tap-resistors.md)
> from 2026-09-19.** Every bias below stays exactly where it is, on the
> **functional** side of the new tap resistors. Each tap then inherits its
> functional net's defined level through the resistor, so no `_INST` net needs a
> pull of its own — but the "every net reaching an `SN74LV541A` input has a
> DC-defining resistor" sweep has to be re-run across the split nets.

**Renumbered and rehomed 2026-09-16.** All eight TMC input biases now live in
`motor_encoder_switch`, next to each other, because what they actually do is
keep the TMC5130A's inputs defined while the bus switch is open — the instrument
taps were always a secondary beneficiary. They were `R1104`-`R1601` in
`instrument_port`; **that sheet now holds none of them.** Note that `R1104` is a
*reused* designator: it previously named the `REFR_DIR` pull-down that was
deleted in favour of a hard GND tie, so older text describing `R1104` is about a
different part.

| Designator | Net             | Termination                               |
|------------|-----------------|-------------------------------------------|
| `R1101`    | `TMC_DIAG0`     | 10 kΩ up to `+3.3V_SW`                    |
| `R1102`    | `TMC_DIAG1`     | 10 kΩ up to `+3.3V_SW`                    |
| `R1103`    | `~{TMC_DRV_EN}` | 10 kΩ up to `+3.3V_SW`                    |
| `R1104`    | `TMC_SPI_SCK`   | 10 kΩ down                                |
| `R1105`    | `TMC_SPI_COPI`  | 10 kΩ down                                |
| `R1106`    | `TMC_SPI_CIPO`  | 10 kΩ down                                |
| `R1107`    | `~{TMC_CS}`     | 10 kΩ up to `+3.3V_SW` — **load-bearing** |
| `R1601`    | `LIMIT_SW`      | 100 kΩ down — **inside the limit-switch block**, correctly: it defines that block's own output |

Nine more are owed by the new blocks, and none of them may live inside a block:
a twin-axis board placing the same block twice would halve every pull, which is
the same argument that keeps `SCL`/`SDA` termination out of the DAC blocks.

| Net                                        | Termination              | Why                                                                       |
|--------------------------------------------|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `DAC_SDA`, `DAC_SCL` (MCU side)            | 4.7 kΩ up to `+3.3V_MCU` | the bus switch is open by default, so the MCU side floats otherwise       |
| `DAC_SDA`, `DAC_SCL` (ISO side)            | 4.7 kΩ up to `+3.3V_SW`  | a switched-domain pull never references the always-on rail                |
| `TQ_SPI_SCK`, `TQ_SPI_COPI`, `TQ_SPI_CIPO` | 10 kΩ down               | the block refuses to terminate; also defines the tap when the ADC is dark |
| `TQ_CONVST_CS`                             | 10 kΩ up to `+3.3V_SW`   | must idle high — load-bearing, same as `~{DAC_CS}` was                    |
| `TQ_CAL_EN`                                | 10 kΩ down               | calibration must be *off*, not floating                                   |

**All fitted as of 2026-09-18, and three more besides.** As built, verified from
the netlist:

| Net | Termination | As built | Sheet |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DAC_SCL_BYP`, `DAC_SDA_BYP` | 4.7 kΩ up to `+3.3V_MCU` | `R402`, `R403` | `/mcu/` |
| `DAC_SCL`, `DAC_SDA` | 4.7 kΩ up to `+3.3V_SW` | `R406`, `R407` | `/mcu/` |
| `TQ_SPI_SCK`, `TQ_SPI_COPI` | 10 kΩ down | `R902`, `R903` | `/brake_torque_sensor/` |
| `TQ_SPI_CIPO` | 10 kΩ down | `R2012` | torque block — correct, see the rule |
| `TQ_CONVST_CS` | 10 kΩ up to `+3.3V_SW` | `R904` | `/brake_torque_sensor/` |
| `TQ_CAL_EN` | 10 kΩ down | `R905` | `/brake_torque_sensor/` |
| `~{BRAKE_FAULT}` | 10 kΩ down | `R901` | `/brake_torque_sensor/` |
| `FW_TRIG0`, `FW_TRIG1` | 10 kΩ down | `R404`, `R405` | `/mcu/` |

The last three are beyond the original nine. `~{BRAKE_FAULT}` belongs to the same
class and was simply missing from the list; the `FW_TRIG` pair closes the final
floating-input window, the ~143 ms between reset and firmware driving the
markers. **Every net reaching an `SN74LV541A` input now has a DC-defining
resistor** — verified by sweeping all 28 of them.

#### Which sheet a pull belongs on

The rule above — *"none of them may live inside a block"* — reads as though it
contradicts the statement further up that *"`LIMIT_SW`, `ENC_A` and `ENC_B` are
defined by pull-downs inside their own blocks."* Both are right. The test is not
which sheet, it is **who drives the net**:

> A pull belongs **inside** a block when it defines that block's own output or an
> internal node. It belongs **at board level** when it biases a net the board
> drives, or shares between blocks.

The reason is placement-count, not electricity: a reusable block instantiated
twice onto one shared bus parallels its internal pulls and halves them. A net the
block alone owns cannot be doubled that way, so its pull is safe inside.

**Board sheets are board level.** `mcu`, `motor_encoder_switch` and
`brake_torque_sensor` are board-owned wrapper sheets, not design blocks — they
exist exactly once, so a termination on any of them satisfies the rule. Choosing
between them is organisational, and grouping a pull with the subsystem it serves
is preferred: it keeps select-by-sheet useful during placement, and these parts
want to sit near the net they define rather than clustered at the MCU.

Every placement on this board follows the rule. Inside their blocks, correctly:
`R1505`/`R1506` (`ENCA`/`ENCB`), `R1601` (`LIMIT_SW`), `R1701` (`PG_5V`),
`R1902`/`R1903` (`PG_12V`) and `R2012` (`TQ_SPI_CIPO`) all define their own
block's output; `R1301`-`R1304` on the buffer `~OE` pins, `R2011` on the ADC's
`~{RST}` and `R607` on `~{BUS_SW_EN}` are internal nodes — `R607` included,
because the RP2040 that drives it lives in that same block.

#### Checking clearance while it is ignored

`rule_severities.clearance` is `ignore` on this project, so DRC cannot report a
clearance violation. **`make clearance-check` restores it on a throwaway copy**
and diffs the result against `kicad/clearance-baseline.json`; the real
`.kicad_pro` is never modified. `make clearance-baseline` re-records the
baseline. Run the baseline before routing and the check after — it exists
because Freerouting's characteristic failure is exactly the class of violation
this board is blind to.

Baseline recorded 2026-09-18, pre-autoroute: **499 clearance findings, 156
unconnected items**, of which **10 net pairs are voltage-bearing** — including
`GND` ↔ `HV_IN` at 0.2331 mm against 0.5 mm required, and `+36V_SW` ↔ `PG_5V` at
0.2919 mm against 0.4 mm. Those are placement, not routing, and an autorouter
will not fix them.

**The check gates only on what is reproducible, and that was measured rather
than assumed.** Three consecutive runs on identical copper gave 499 findings
every time but attributed them across 149, 151 and 148 net pairs, with 10 of
~270 positions moving: KiCad's DRC picks a different counterpart item where nets
crowd. Stable across runs, and therefore what fails the check: the total count,
the voltage-bearing subset, the unconnected count, and the non-clearance
violation tallies. The per-pair breakdown is printed for orientation only.
`--all-track-errors` is passed for the same reason — without it KiCad reports
one error per track and the choice varies.

**Corrected 2026-09-18:** `TQ_CAL_EN` and `TQ_CONVST_CS` were pulled from inside
the torque block, which was wrong — both are MCU-driven inputs. They are now
`R905` and `R904` on `/brake_torque_sensor/`. Removing them cascade-renumbered
the whole `20xx` band and shifted `R901`-`R903`; the electrical topology was
confirmed unchanged by comparing every net-pair and value before and after.

**4.7 kΩ, not the 2.2 kΩ the analog block's note suggests** — that note is right
for *one* segment and this board has two in parallel the moment the bus switch
closes. Use `OW-RES-4K7-0402`, four of them; the catalog entry is already
annotated for exactly this.

The arithmetic, with measured part capacitances rather than a guess. Switched
segment: two `DAC80501` at **10 pF max per pin** (DACx0501 datasheet), the
`SN74LV541A` tap at 2 pF, the `SN74CB3Q3245` channel at **11 pF max** `Cio(ON)`,
plus ~12 pF of trace — about **45 pF**. MCU segment: an RP2040 pad and a short
run, about **15 pF**. Connected, call it **70 pF** with margin.

| Pull-ups per side | Effective when connected | t_r = 0.8473·R·C at 70 pF | Sink to hold 0.4 V                  |
|-------------------|--------------------------|---------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| 2.2 kΩ            | 1.1 kΩ                   | 65 ns                     | **2.64 mA — 88% of the 3 mA floor** |
| **4.7 kΩ**        | **2.35 kΩ**              | **139 ns**                | **1.23 mA**                         |
| 10 kΩ             | 5.0 kΩ                   | 297 ns — at the limit     | 0.58 mA                             |

Fast mode allows 300 ns of rise and the I²C-bus specification requires a device
to sink 3 mA at `V_OL` ≤ 0.4 V; the DACx0501 datasheet specifies no `V_OL` at
all, it only requires an external pull-up, so that 3 mA is the floor. 4.7 kΩ
clears both with room at 400 kHz, which is the design target — the analog
block's 987 Hz reconstruction filter caps the useful update rate near 2 kHz, so
fast-mode-plus buys nothing here. If it were ever wanted, 3.3 kΩ per side gives
98 ns and 1.76 mA, at the cost of a new internal part.

**A third reason to stay at 4.7 kΩ rather than going lower:** if firmware ever
closes the bus switch with `+3.3V_SW` down, the MCU-side pull-ups feed the dead
DACs' input clamps. 4.7 kΩ bounds that to ~0.6 mA per line instead of handing it
an unlimited source. It does not make the sequencing error safe — it makes it
survivable.

**Neither pair is optional.** The MCU-side pair is what defines `GPIO16`/`GPIO17`
while the bus is open; the RP2040's internal 50-80 kΩ pull-ups are a
firmware-dependent second layer, not a substitute. The switched-side pair must
reference `+3.3V_SW` so both lines sit at a true 0 V when that rail is down —
which is simultaneously what gives the always-on `DIG21`/`DIG22` taps a defined
low, and why those two channels need no pull-downs of their own.

**Before adding a `~{BRAKE_FAULT}` pull-up, check the brake block's netlist** —
`R36001` or `R36017` may already be it, and a second one in parallel halves it.

### The Encoder And Limit Switch Do Not Reach The MCU

**Decided 2026-08-16.** `ENC_A`, `ENC_B`, and `LIMIT_SW` are the TMC5130A's
business. The encoder goes from `J1103` through the board's conditioning chain to
`ENCA`/`ENCB`; the debounced limit switch goes to `REFL`. **Neither reaches an
RP2040 pin, in any revision.** Firmware gets position from the driver's
`X_ENC`/`XACTUAL` register and homing state from the driver's status, both over
SPI.

**There is no `ENC_N` net on the board.** Earlier drafts of this section listed
one alongside `ENC_A`/`ENC_B`; as built (2026-08-17) `J1103` pin 2 is a reserved
index **no-connect** and the TMC5130A's `ENCN` pin is terminated by `R1201` 10 kΩ
to GND, which is what the datasheet asks for on an unused encoder input. The
index is a rev-1 decision, not a Rev 0 signal.

This frees `GP14`, `GP15`, `GP16`, and `GP18`. `GP14` was spent again on
2026-08-17 on `HV_DIAG_EN`.

**What it deletes, permanently rather than deferring:**

- The **RP2040 PIO encoder cross-check**. It is not "rev 1" any more, it is gone.
- **`ENCODER_MISMATCH`** in `docs/uart-protocol.md`. There is no second count to
  disagree with and there never will be, so the fault code should be retired
  rather than left reserved.
- The `GP14`/`GP15`/`GP16` **contiguity constraint**. It existed only to let one
  PIO state machine read A, B, and the index with a single input mapping. Those
  three pins are now ordinary spares with no adjacency requirement — which is
  precisely what made `GP14` available for `HV_DIAG_EN` on 2026-08-17.
- The MCU's **independent copy of the limit switch**. Firmware learns a homing
  event from the driver, one SPI poll later than the hardware `REFL` latch — which
  is the same latency the design already accepted, since `REFL` was always the
  hardware path and `GP18` was always just a witness.

**What replaces the witness:** the InstrumentPort. `ENC_A`, `ENC_B`, and
`LIMIT_SW` are all on it in Rev 0, which is now the *only* way to see those
signals independently of the driver's own report. That is a stronger reason for
them to be on the port than existed when the MCU also had copies.

> **Settled 2026-09-16 and it no longer "fits with room".** What was rev-2
> planning is now the v1.0 allocation above: brake and torque cost **eight** pins
> between them, not six — `SDA`, `SCL`, `~{BRAKE_FAULT}`, three for `SPI1`,
> `TQ_CONVST_CS` and `TQ_CAL_EN` — and `HV_LATCH` took the last spare after
> that. One pin is left, `GP27`, and it is ADC-capable. **The paragraphs below
> are the arithmetic that got us here and every one of their premises has since
> changed**: the brake is I2C with no chip select, so `~{BRAKE_CS}` does not
> exist; `~{BRAKE_FAULT}` is not optional; the current monitor stays off the MCU
> entirely; and the torque bus needs five pins, not two. Read them as history.

**Rev 2 fits on RP2040 with room, as of 2026-08-26.** Full scope is 24 of 30
with six spares, and the brake plus torque front end for a single axis needs
about six GPIOs — `BRAKE_DIM`, `~{BRAKE_FAULT}`, a brake current monitor on ADC,
two for the torque bus, and `TQ_DRDY`. That is **six wanted against six spare**
even keeping `TQ_DRDY`, with `GP27` ADC-capable for the current monitor. Drop
`TQ_DRDY`, which the bus capture already implies, and there is a pin left over.

**Got easier 2026-08-31.** The settled brake driver needs **one** new GPIO, not
two or three: `~{BRAKE_CS}` for its DAC, sharing `SCK` and `SDI` with the angle
DAC — both are write-only 3-wire devices, so bus sharing carries no contention
risk. `~{BRAKE_FAULT}` is optional and only exists if the `SN74LVC2G17` fault
buffer is populated; `BRAKE_ENABLE` is a stuffing option and largely redundant
with `HV_EN`. So the brake side is **1 GPIO plus 1 ADC**, against the 3 GPIOs plus
1 ADC this paragraph budgeted. That leaves more slack for the torque bus, which is
where it is actually wanted.

**This reversed twice.** Until `GP14` became `HV_DIAG_EN` on 2026-08-17 it was
five for five with nothing to reclaim; that day it became five wanted against
four spare, one pin short of free, and the fix was to spend reclaim-order item 1.
On 2026-08-26 the analog output block landed on a part with no `LDAC` or `CLR`
pin and returned `GP12` and `GP17` for nothing, which closes the gap outright
rather than by trading a function away. **Reclaim-order item 1 is now void** —
see below.

**The twin-axis board needs RP2354B because it carries two of everything; this
board may not.** Do not treat that as settled — it is an observation to check
when the rev 2 circuits are actually specified, not a commitment. It is a
stronger observation than it was, but the rev 2 circuits are still unspecified.

### What The Rail Sense Is Actually For

**`GP26` senses `+3.3V_SW` through a ÷2 divider as of 2026-08-16**, replacing a
divided `+5V_SW` sense. Same two resistors, better measurement — sensing the end
of the chain confirms 36 V, 5 V, and 3.3 V in one reading, and `+3.3V_SW` is the
rail that actually gates the decision, because it is what powers the far side of
the bus switch.

**Where the divider physically sits, as built 2026-08-17.** The `mcu` sheet pin
called `SW_RAIL_SENSE` carries the **raw** `+3.3V_SW` rail across the sheet
boundary; `R408`/`R409` (1 kΩ/1 kΩ) divide it *inside* `mcu`, and the ADC pin sees
`SW_RAIL_SENSE_DIV_2`. Two consequences worth holding on to. The `mcu` sheet pin
is therefore a rail tap, not a signal, so do not expect a 1.65 V node at the sheet
boundary. And **`R408`/`R409` are also what holds `+3.3V_SW` at 0 V when the
switched domain is off** — a 2 kΩ bleed to GND — which is the property the
board-level pull-ups to `+3.3V_SW` depend on. Removing the divider would leave
`~{TMC_CS}`, both `DIAG` lines, and `~{TMC_DRV_EN}` undefined in the off state.

**Why not delete it, given the TMC answers SPI when the rails are up?** Because of
a circularity. `docs/power.md` makes the rail sense one of three supporting
measures for the isolation architecture: *reconnect only after the rails are
confirmed up*. SPI reaches the TMC5130A **through the bus switch you are deciding
whether to enable**, so it cannot confirm anything before that decision. Enabling
the bus into an unpowered driver is precisely the back-power failure the whole
architecture exists to prevent. The sense must bypass the bus switch, and `GP26`
does.

**It is substantially redundant with `HV_SNS`**, though, and that is worth knowing
if the pin is ever wanted elsewhere. `GP28` also bypasses the bus switch, and the
buck, the LDO, and the driver draw quiescent current whenever the rail is really
up, so a near-zero `HV_SNS` after raising `HV_EN` already means "the rail did not
come up." Gating on `HV_SNS` plus a timeout would be defensible.

**`~{HV_FAULT}` does not cover this**, and it is worth being explicit about why:
with no 36 V present the `TPS1HTC100-Q1` is itself unpowered, so its open-drain
fault output floats and the pull-up reads it as *no fault*. The most likely
failure on the bench — nobody plugged the supply in — is invisible to `~{HV_FAULT}`
and obvious to either `SW_RAIL_SENSE` or `HV_SNS`.

**Firmware rule:** after raising `HV_EN`, confirm `SW_RAIL_SENSE_DIV_2` reads a
valid `+3.3V_SW` before deasserting `~{BUS_SW_EN}`. Refuse `ARM` with a specific
reason when it does not, and report the reading in `STATUS`.

### Signal Direction And Sheet Pin Types

**A hierarchical pin's direction is stated from the point of view of the sheet
that owns it.** `Output` means the signal leaves this sheet; `Input` means it
enters. The same net is `Output` on the sheet that drives it and `Input` on every
sheet that reads it. Nothing about the direction is global — `TMC_SPI_SCK` is an
`Output` on `mcu` and an `Input` on the `tmc5130` sheet, and both are correct.

#### `DIO-A` Is This Board's RX. `DIO-B` Is This Board's TX.

This is the one crossover on the board that reliably gets wired backwards, and
the trap is that the alphabetical order reverses:

```
  RJ-45 pin 1   DIO-A   host TX  ──▶  PYC_DIO_A  ──▶  PYC_UART_RX  ──▶  GP1  (UART0 RX)
  RJ-45 pin 4   DIO-B   host RX  ◀──  PYC_DIO_B  ◀──  PYC_UART_TX  ◀──  GP0  (UART0 TX)
```

`A` → `RX`, `B` → `TX`. Both names are right; they are named from different ends.
The pyControl block names its pins by **connector position** on purpose, so a
board cannot mirror them by accident — that is exactly what the block's own
description warns about. This board names its nets by **MCU function**. The
crossover happens once, at the `mcu` sheet boundary, and nowhere else.

Sanity check that needs no documentation: `PYC_UART_TX` must be an `Output` on
`mcu`. If a sheet pin named `*_TX` is an `Input`, it is wrong.
